messages:
deploy-bot: Starting canary rollout for release v2.3.14 to 5% of traffic in us-west-2. policy=canary-health-probes

incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: canary_health_probe_failures threshold exceeded (5xx rate > 4% over 2m) for service=runtime-api, shard=canary-usw2-1. paging on-call.

Sam L: saw this on dashboards, 5xx spike up to ~6% on the canary nodes, latency slightly elevated.

Priya K: on it, pinging logs. canary group size = 6 pods, 3 failing health probes right now.

Aisha R: any customer impact seen yet?

Elena (Support): one support ticket from EU reporting errors on generation requests; might be unrelated but times align.

Tom S: checking probe logs: 502s coming from model shard timeouts, stack traces show `kv-cache miss -> backend timeout 10s`.

Ben C: rollback criteria in runbook: if canary 5xx > 5% for 3 consecutive minutes OR more than 20% of canary instances fail health checks -> abort. We're at 6% now, 2 consecutive minutes.

Priya K: starting canary_abort procedure. marking as P1. tagging SRE pager.

Sam L: can we flip feature flag to kill risky path? feature flag `enable_kv_prefetch_v2` was included in this release. Try disabling first?

Tom S: good call. issuing flag toggle now: `flagsctl set enable_kv_prefetch_v2 false --env=canary-usw2`

deploy-bot: Feature flag disable command accepted. propagation to canary env in progress.

Priya K: flag propagated to 4/6 canary pods, observing decrease in errors on those nodes. 2 pods still failing.

incident-bot: NOTE: Abort criteria still met (5xx > 5%). Runbook suggests abort + rollback when flag flip doesn't fix within 5m.

Sam L: starting graceful abort: `redwoodctl rollout abort --release v2.3.14 --target canary-usw2`

Tom S: running healthcheck sweep: `for p in $(kubectl get pods -l role=canary -o name); do kubectl exec $p -- curl -sS -I localhost:8080/health || echo $p fail; done`

Ben C: abort command acknowledged by deploy system. canary traffic will be drained over 30s and switched back to baseline model variant.

Elena (Support): I've posted a short note to support channel: "We observed elevated errors during a canary rollout in us-west-2; rollback initiated, working with infra. If you see customer reports, escalate to oncall."

Priya K: confirming rollback: `redwoodctl rollout rollback --release v2.3.14 --to-version v2.3.13 --confirm` executed.

deploy-bot: Rollback started. Expected completion ~T+2m. Healthcheck endpoints returning 200 on restored pods.

Sam L: monitoring metrics — 5xx count dropping back to baseline (~0.2%). Latency stabilizing.

Aisha R: any idea root cause? The kv-prefetch change looked safe in staging.

Tom S: early hypothesis: under production traffic pattern the prefetch path induced concurrent KV cache pressure and caused backend timeouts; we saw increase in backend queue lengths on the canary nodes only.

Ben C: will open a follow-up incident with postmortem tasks: reproduce with production-like load, add stronger prefetched write backpressure, add circuit-breaker around KV backend.

Priya K: oncall handoff note: taking a quick runbook step to ensure all canary pods are back to baseline and global rollout prevented. leaving the thread open for postmortem owners.

Sam L: marking incident as mitigated. assigning postmortem to Tom S and Ben C. ETA for initial write-up 48h.

incident-bot: Incident PAGER cleared. Severity: P2 (canary-only, short-lived customer errors).

Elena (Support): I informed the affected customer that we rolled back and are investigating; they replied they saw transient failures but are okay for now.

Priya K: action items: (1) add more strict canary probe on kv-latency (2) add abort-on-kv-timeout to canary policy (3) run a stress test with prefetch enabled against prod-like KV dataset.

Tom S: copying commands used to abort/rollback in case someone needs them later:
```
redwoodctl rollout abort --release v2.3.14 --target canary-usw2
redwoodctl rollout rollback --release v2.3.14 --to-version v2.3.13 --confirm
flagsctl set enable_kv_prefetch_v2 false --env=canary-usw2
kubectl get pods -l role=canary -o name
```

Sam L: thanks everyone. leaving channel for next on-call in 10m. handoff: Priya -> Ben. Ben you got this? :eyes:

Ben C: got it. will own postmortem and the follow-ups. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: On-call handoff recorded: from Priya K to Ben C. thread closed for active paging.

(reacted :thumbsup: by Sam L, Priya K)
